translations.text: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
My angel before your face, who will prepare your way. And immediately many gathered, so that there was no room, not even in front of the door. And he spoke the word to them.
The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: “Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.”
John came baptizing in the wilderness and preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
And the Judean countryside and the people of Jerusalem went out to him, and they were all baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
John was clothed in camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.
And he preached, saying, “One stronger than I is coming after me. I am not worthy to stoop down and untie the strap of his sandals.
I have baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”
Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
And immediately, as he came up out of the water, he saw the heavens opening and the Spirit descending upon him like a dove.
And a voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son; I am well pleased with you.”
At that time, Jesus went out to a deserted place and stayed there.
And Simon and those who were with him went after him.
And when they found him, they said to him, “Everyone is looking for you.”
And he said to them, “Let us go to the nearby villages and towns, so that I may preach there too, for that is why I came out.”
And he preached in their synagogues throughout Galilee and drove out demons.
And a leper came to him, pleading with him and falling to his knees, and said to him, “If you are willing, you can make me clean.”
Jesus, moved with compassion, stretched out his hand, touched him, and said to him, “I am willing. Be clean.”
And when he had said this, the leprosy immediately left the man, and he became clean.
And he sternly warned him and sent him away.
And he said to him, “See that you say nothing to anyone. Instead, go and show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
At that time, Jesus entered Capernaum, and word spread that he was in the house.
As it is written in the prophets: “Behold, I will send
And they came to him bringing a paralyzed man, carried by four people.
And because they could not get near him because of the crowd, they removed the roof where he was, and after digging through it, they lowered the bed on which the paralyzed man lay.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralyzed man, “Child, your sins are forgiven.”
Some of the scribes were sitting there, thinking in their hearts,
“Why does this man speak such blasphemies? Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
Jesus immediately knew in his spirit that they were thinking this within themselves, and he said to them, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?
Which is easier: to say to the paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority to forgive sins on earth”—he said to the paralyzed man,
“I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
He immediately got up, picked up his mat, and went out in front of everyone. They were all amazed and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”
At that time, as Jesus was passing by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth. He said to him, “Follow me.” And he got up and followed him.
As Jesus reclined at the table in his house, many tax collectors and sinners reclined with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many, and they followed him.

When the scribes and Pharisees saw him eating with tax collectors and sinners, they said to his disciples, “Why is it that with tax collectors and sinners”—they said to his disciples, “Why is it that he eats and drinks with tax collectors and sinners?”
When Jesus heard this, he said to them, “Those who are healthy do not need a doctor, but those who are sick do. For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
At that time, Jesus was walking through the grainfields on the Sabbath, and his disciples began to make their way along, plucking heads of grain.
The Pharisees said to him, “Look, why is he doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?”
He said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he was in need and was hungry, he and those who were with him?
How he entered the house of God when Abiathar was high priest and ate the bread of the Presence, which no one but the priests was permitted to eat?”
And he said to them, “The Sabbath was made for humankind, not humankind for the Sabbath.
Therefore the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
He entered the synagogue again, and a man with a withered hand was there.
They watched him to see whether he would heal the man on the Sabbath, so that they could bring an accusation against him.
He said to the man with the withered hand, “Stand here in the midst of them.”
And he said to them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy it?” But they remained silent.
He looked around at them with anger, grieving at the hardness of their hearts, and said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored, as sound as the other.
At that time, Jesus wished to go into Galilee. He found Philip and said to him, “Follow me.”
Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.
Philip found Nathanael and said to him, “We have found the one Moses wrote about in the Law, and the prophets also wrote about: Jesus, the son of Joseph, from Nazareth.”
Nathanael said to him, “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.”
Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him and said to him, “Here is a true Israelite, in whom there is no deceit.”
Nathanael said to him, “How do you know me?” Jesus answered him, “Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree.”
Nathanael answered him, “Teacher, you are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!”
Jesus answered him, “Do you believe because I told you that I saw you under the fig tree? You will see greater things than these.”
And he said to him, “Truly, truly, I tell you all, from now on you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.”
At that time, a large crowd was following Jesus and pressing against him.
And there was a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years.
She had suffered greatly under physicians and had spent everything she had, but had gained no benefit and had instead grown worse.
Having heard about Jesus, she came up behind him and touched his garment.
For she said, “If I touch his garment, I will be healed.”
Immediately the source of her bleeding dried up, and she knew in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
Immediately Jesus, sensing within himself that power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd and said, “Who touched my clothes?”
His disciples said to him, “You see the crowd pressing against you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
And he looked around to see the woman who had done this.
But the woman, frightened and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before him and told him the whole truth.
Jesus said, “Your faith has healed you. Go in peace.”
At that time, Jesus left the regions of Tyre and Sidon and came to the Sea of Galilee, within the territory of the Decapolis.
They brought him a deaf man who had difficulty speaking and begged him to lay his hand on him.
He took him aside, away from the crowd, put his finger into the man’s ears, and spat and touched his tongue.
Looking up to heaven, he sighed and said to him, “Ephphatha,” which means, “Be opened.”
Immediately his ears were opened, the bond on his tongue was loosened, and he spoke clearly.
He ordered them not to tell anyone. But the more he ordered them not to, the more they proclaimed it.
They were utterly amazed and said, “He does everything well. He even makes the deaf hear and the mute speak.”
At that time, Jesus and his disciples went out to the villages of Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked his disciples, “Who do people say I am?”
They answered him, “Some say John the Baptist, others Elijah, and others one of the prophets.”
Jesus said to them, “But who do you say I am?” Peter answered him, “You are the Christ.”
And he warned them not to tell anyone about him.
And he began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer greatly, be put to the test by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, be killed, and rise on the third day.
The Lord said to his disciples, “Whoever wants to follow me must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake and for the gospel will save it.
For what does it profit a person to gain the whole world and forfeit his soul?
For what can a person give in exchange for his soul?
For whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.”
And he said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, there are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God come in power.”
At that time, a man came to Jesus, bowing before him and saying, “Teacher, I brought my son to you. He has a mute and deaf spirit.
Whenever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and becomes rigid. I told your disciples to drive it out, but they could not.”
He said to them, “O unbelieving generation, how long will I be with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring him to me.”
And they brought him to him. When the spirit saw him, it convulsed the boy, and he fell to the ground and rolled about, foaming at the mouth.
Jesus asked his father, “How long has this been happening to him?” He answered him, “Since childhood.
It has often thrown him into fire and into water to drown him. But if you are willing, help me and have compassion on me.”
Jesus said to him, “If you can believe, all things are possible for the one who believes.”
Immediately the child’s father cried out with tears, saying, “I believe, Lord! Help my unbelief!”
When Jesus saw that a crowd was gathering, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, “Mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him!”
And after crying out and convulsing him violently, it came out. He became like a dead person, and many said, “He will die.”
But Jesus took him by the hand, raised him, and set him on his feet.
When he had entered the house, his disciples asked him privately, “Why could we not drive it out?”
And he said to them, “This kind can come out by nothing except prayer and fasting.”
They left that place and traveled through Galilee, and he did not want anyone to know.
For he was teaching his disciples and telling them, “The Son of Man will be handed over into human hands, and they will kill him. After being killed, he will rise on the third day.”
At that time, Jesus took his twelve disciples aside and began to tell them what was going to happen to him.
“Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn him to death and hand him over to the Gentiles.
They will mock him and beat him, and on the third day he will rise.”
James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came before him and said to him, “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask.”
Jesus said to them, “What do you want me to do for you?”
They said to him, “Grant that we may sit in your glory, one at your right and the other at your left.”
Jesus said to them, “You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I drink, or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?”
They said to him, “We can.” Jesus said to them, “You will indeed drink the cup that I drink, and you will be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized.
But to sit at my right or at my left is not mine to grant; it is for those for whom it has been prepared.”
When the ten heard this, they began to be indignant with James and John.
Jesus called them to him and said to them, “You know that those who are considered rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great men exercise authority over them.
But it is not so among you.
Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be the servant of all, and whoever wants to be first among you must be the slave of all.
For the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
At that time, the soldiers led Jesus into the courtyard of Caiaphas, which is the Praetorium, and called together the whole cohort.
They clothed him in purple, twisted together a crown of thorns, and put it on him.
They began to salute him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”
They struck him on the head with a reed, spat on him, and bowed down before him.
When they had mocked him, they stripped the purple robe off him, dressed him in his own clothes, and led him out to crucify him.
They compelled a passerby, Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the countryside, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry his cross.
They brought him to the place called Golgotha, which means “Place of the Skull.”
They offered him sour wine to drink, and he accepted it.
After crucifying him, they divided his clothes, casting lots for them to decide who would take what.
It was the third hour when they crucified him.
And the inscription stating the charge against him was written: “This is the King of the Jews.”
And they crucified two robbers with him, one on his right and the other on his left.
And the scripture was fulfilled that says, “And he was counted among the lawless.”
And those passing by insulted him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,
save yourself, and come down from the cross yourself!”
Likewise, the chief priests also mocked him with the scribes, saying to one another, “He saved others, but he cannot save himself.
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe.”
